articles.summary: Planning ahead and accounting for more than gifts can help consumers stay on budget throughout the holiday season St. Louis, MO (November 10, 2026) Financial experts say a little extra planning this holiday season can help families account for everyday costs while keeping gifts, travel, and celebrations enjoyable. According to First Mid Bank Trust Chief Retail Banking Officer Stas Wolak, holiday costs extend well beyond presents. A full grocery cart for a family meal, a few tanks of gas, higher utility use, plane tickets, restaurant tabs, decorations, shipping charges, and wrapping supplies can often rival the gift budget. Before the first gift is purchased, inflation has already taken a seat at the holiday table. The biggest financial surprise during the holidays is often not what people buy for others its all the additional expenses that come with celebrating, Wolak said. None of these expenses look overwhelming by themselves. Together,
articles.title: First Mid Bank & Trust Shares Tips for Managing Holiday Spending Amid Rising Costs
